chunks: As for what Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muskan, from Ayyub ibn al-Hurr, who said:
Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who died while he was on a ship at sea: what should be done with him?
He said: 'He is to be placed in a clay jar (khābiya), its mouth sealed, and cast into the water.'

The correct interpretation of this narration is that it should be understood as a type of recommended (mustahabb) practice when one has the ability to do so, and the earlier narrations as applying to cases where this is not feasible, thereby lifting the prohibition.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommended practice (mustahabb); a non-obligatory yet praiseworthy act in Islamic law
key_terms.تَعَذُّرِ: impossibility; impracticability of carrying out an act due to circumstances
key_terms.خَابِيَةٍ: clay jar; a large earthen vessel used here as a container for sea burial
key_terms.رَفْعِ الْحَظْرِ: lifting of the prohibition; jurisprudential formula indicating permissibility when necessity applies

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rule about a person who dies on a ship at sea, and how does Shaykh al-Tusi reconcile this hadith with earlier narrations?
ai.summary: Ayyub ibn al-Hurr narrates that Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who dies aboard a ship at sea, and the Imam ruled that the body should be placed in a clay jar (khābiya), its mouth sealed, and cast into the water. Shaykh al-Tusi reconciles this ruling with earlier narrations by interpreting the present hadith as indicating a recommended (mustahabb) practice when it is feasible, while the earlier narrations apply when placing the body in a jar is impossible, thereby lifting the prohibition on direct sea disposal.
